question: As per Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2022, India ranks at ______ position.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 107th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• GHI 2022 released by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe; India ranked 107th out of 121 countries. (हरित भूख सूचकांक)

 

• India's GHI 2022 score was 29.1, placing it in the "serious" hunger category.

 

• India ranked behind several neighbours, including Pakistan (99), Bangladesh (84), Nepal (81), and Sri Lanka (64).

 

• GHI is calculated using four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, and child mortality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The GHI report has been published annually since 2006 by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany).

 

• In the 2023 GHI, India's rank slipped further to 111th out of 125 countries.

 

NOTE

 

• 57th (Option 1): not India's actual GHI 2022 rank; far better than India's real position.

 

• 77th (Option 2): not India's actual GHI 2022 rank.

 

• 97th (Option 3): not India's actual rank; close to Pakistan's rank (99) but not India's.

question: What is the full form of EPROM?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• EPROM full form: Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory. (प्रोग्राम करने योग्य केवल पढ़े जाने वाली स्मृति)

 

• It is a type of non-volatile memory chip that retains stored data even when power is switched off.

 

• Data on classic EPROM chips can be erased by exposing them to strong ultraviolet (UV) light and then reprogrammed.

 

• EPROM is a successor to PROM (Programmable ROM) and a precursor to EEPROM (Electrically Erasable PROM).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ROM family includes: PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, and Flash memory.

 

• Modern flash memory (used in USB drives, SSDs, memory cards) evolved from EEPROM technology.

 

NOTE

 

• Erasable Permanent Read Only Memory (Option 1): incorrect expansion; the word "Programmable" is missing and "Permanent" is not part of the correct term.

 

• Entire Programmable Read Only Memory (Option 2): incorrect; the correct first word is "Erasable," not "Entire."

 

• Entire Permanent Read Only Memory (Option 4): incorrect on both counts; neither "Entire" nor "Permanent" are part of the correct expansion.

question: Which of the following is monoatomic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Helium is a noble/inert gas that exists as single, uncombined atoms — i.e., it is monoatomic. (हीलियम - एकपरमाण्विक गैस)

 

• All noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) have a complete outer electron shell, so their atoms do not combine with one another to form molecules.

 

• Nitrogen (N₂), Oxygen (O₂) and Chlorine (Cl₂) all exist as diatomic molecules under normal conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ozone (O₃) is a triatomic form of oxygen.

 

• Phosphorus commonly exists as P₄ (tetra-atomic) and Sulphur as S₈ (poly-atomic) in their elemental forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option 1): a diatomic gas, exists in nature as N₂ molecules.

 

• Oxygen (Option 2): a diatomic gas, exists in nature as O₂ molecules.

 

• Chlorine (Option 3): a diatomic gas, exists in nature as Cl₂ molecules.

question: Which of the following persons has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kailash Satyarthi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian child-rights activist, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Malala Yousafzai of Pakistan. (कैलाश सत्यार्थी - नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार)

 

• He founded the Bachpan Bachao Andolan (Save the Childhood Movement) to campaign against child labour and for children's right to education.

 

• He is only the second Indian, after Mother Teresa (1979), to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for discovering the Raman Effect.

 

• Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (1998); Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913) for Gitanjali.

 

NOTE

 

• C. V. Raman (Option 1): Nobel laureate in Physics, not Peace.

 

• Amartya Sen (Option 3): Nobel laureate in Economic Sciences, not Peace.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 4): Nobel laureate in Literature, not Peace.

question: Gandhiji, aged ______, arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 46.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915, at the age of 46. (महात्मा गांधी - दक्षिण अफ्रीका से भारत वापसी)

 

• This date is now commemorated every year as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (NRI Day).

 

• Gandhi had spent about 21 years in South Africa (1893-1914), where he developed the technique of Satyagraha.

 

• His political mentor Gopal Krishna Gokhale advised him to travel across India for a year to understand the country before taking up any leadership role.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's first major involvement in Indian politics after his return was the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar.

 

• 9 January has been celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas since 2003.

 

NOTE

 

• 52 (Option 1): incorrect; Gandhi was younger than this when he returned to India in 1915.

 

• 28 (Option 3): incorrect; this was roughly his age when he first travelled to South Africa in 1893.

 

• 34 (Option 4): incorrect age for the time of his return to India in 1915.

question: Which among the following is a viral disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chicken pox.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chicken pox is caused by the Varicella-zoster virus, making it a viral disease. (चिकन पॉक्स - विषाणु जनित रोग)

 

• It is a highly contagious disease characterised by itchy, blister-like skin rashes.

 

• Tuberculosis and Whooping Cough are bacterial diseases, caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* and *Bordetella pertussis* respectively.

 

• Malaria is caused by *Plasmodium*, a protozoan parasite transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common viral diseases include Measles, Mumps, Influenza, COVID-19, Dengue and Polio.

 

• The Chicken pox (Varicella) vaccine is part of the routine immunization schedule in many countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Tuberculosis (Option 2): a bacterial disease caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*.

 

• Whooping Cough (Option 3): a bacterial disease caused by *Bordetella pertussis*.

 

• Malaria (Option 4): a parasitic disease caused by the protozoan *Plasmodium*.

question: Which of the following is NOT a valid file format in MS-PowerPoint 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is .pwpt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ".pwpt" is not a valid or recognised file extension used by MS-PowerPoint. (अमान्य फाइल प्रारूप)

 

• ".ppt" is the default file format for PowerPoint presentations up to the 2003 version.

 

• ".pptx" is the XML-based default format used from PowerPoint 2007 onwards.

 

• ".pptm" is a macro-enabled PowerPoint presentation format.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other valid PowerPoint formats include .ppsx (PowerPoint Show), .potx (PowerPoint Template), and .thmx (PowerPoint Theme).

 

• MS-PowerPoint 365 is the subscription-based version of Microsoft's presentation software, part of Microsoft 365 (Office 365).

 

NOTE

 

• .pptm (Option 1): a valid, macro-enabled PowerPoint presentation format.

 

• .ppt (Option 3): a valid, legacy PowerPoint presentation format.

 

• .pptx (Option 4): a valid, standard XML-based PowerPoint presentation format.

question: The First Amendment Act, 1951 of the Indian constitution added which of the following schedules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ninth schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951 inserted Articles 31A and 31B and added the Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution. (नौवीं अनुसूची)

 

• The Ninth Schedule was created mainly to protect land reform and other laws from judicial review under Article 31B.

 

• In the I.R. Coelho case (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 (the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment) are open to judicial review.

 

• The First Amendment Act also amended Articles 15, 19 and 85.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.

 

• The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; it now has 12 Schedules.

 

NOTE

 

• Tenth schedule (Option 1): deals with anti-defection provisions, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.

 

• Eleventh schedule (Option 3): deals with the powers of Panchayats, added by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992.

 

• Seventh schedule (Option 4): deals with the division of powers between Union, State and Concurrent Lists — part of the original Constitution of 1950.

question: The asteroid belt lies between which two planets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mars and Jupiter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The asteroid belt is a torus-shaped region located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. (क्षुद्रग्रह पट्टी - मंगल और बृहस्पति के बीच)

 

• It contains millions of asteroids/minor planets — remnants from the early formation of the solar system that never coalesced into a planet due to Jupiter's gravitational influence.

 

• Ceres, the largest object in the asteroid belt, is classified as a dwarf planet.

 

• The asteroid belt is sometimes called the "Main Belt" to distinguish it from other groups like the Kuiper Belt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kuiper Belt lies beyond Neptune's orbit and contains icy bodies, including Pluto.

 

• NASA's Dawn mission studied Vesta and Ceres, two of the largest objects in the asteroid belt.

 

NOTE

 

• Jupiter and Saturn (Option 1): no major asteroid belt lies here; this region instead contains the two planets' own moon systems.

 

• Saturn and Uranus (Option 3): not the location of the main asteroid belt.

 

• Mercury and Venus (Option 4): no asteroid belt exists in this inner region of the solar system.

question: Which among the following is not an All India Financial Institution?
option_2: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is ICICI Bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs) are specialised financial institutions regulated by the RBI that provide long-term finance to specific sectors of the economy. (अखिल भारतीय वित्तीय संस्थान)

 

• The AIFIs regulated by RBI include NABARD, NHB, EXIM Bank, and SIDBI (and, since 2021, also NaBFID).

 

• ICICI Bank is a private-sector scheduled commercial bank, not an AIFI.

 

• AIFIs primarily provide refinance and developmental support to their respective sectors, rather than regular retail/commercial banking services.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD — apex institution for agriculture and rural development, established 1982.

 

• NHB — apex institution for housing finance, established 1988; EXIM Bank — apex institution for foreign trade financing, established 1982.

 

NOTE

 

• National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Option 2): an AIFI that regulates and refinances rural credit institutions.

 

• National Housing Bank (Option 3): an AIFI that regulates and refinances housing finance companies.

 

• Export - Import Bank of India (Option 4): an AIFI that finances and promotes India's foreign trade.

question: Qawwali was brought in India from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Persia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Qawwali, a devotional Sufi music genre, was brought to India from Persia. (क़व्वाली - फारस से भारत में लाई गई)

 

• It is traced to Amir Khusrau (13th century), who is credited with fusing Persian, Arabic, Turkish and Indian musical traditions to create Qawwali.

 

• The word "Qawwali" comes from the Arabic word "Qaul," meaning "utterance" or "saying (of the Prophet)."

 

• Qawwali is traditionally performed at Sufi shrines (dargahs), especially those associated with the Chishti order.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan is one of the most renowned Qawwali singers of modern times.

 

• Amir Khusrau is also popularly credited with the development of instruments like the sitar and tabla.

 

NOTE

 

• Turkey (Option 1): not the region credited with introducing Qawwali to India.

 

• Mongolia (Option 2): not associated with the origin of Qawwali.

 

• Saudi Arabia (Option 3): not the specific region credited, though the term "Qawwali" itself has Arabic roots.

question: Which country won the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ukraine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ukraine won the 2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup, held in Poland, defeating South Korea 3-1 in the final. (यूक्रेन - फीफा अंडर-20 विश्व कप 2019 विजेता)

 

• This was Ukraine's first FIFA U-20 World Cup title.

 

• The tournament was hosted by Poland from 23 May to 15 June 2019.

 

• Serhiy Buletsa of Ukraine was named the tournament's best player (Golden Ball).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ukraine's win came after a dramatic comeback in the final, having trailed South Korea 1-0.

 

• The Golden Boot (top scorer of the tournament) went to Israel's Dor Peretz.

 

NOTE

 

• Poland (Option 1): hosted the tournament but did not win it.

 

• Norway (Option 2): did not win the 2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

 

• South Korea (Option 4): runner-up in the 2019 final, lost to Ukraine.

question: The approximate length of the Great Himalayan range, also known as the central axial range, is ______ km from east to west.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2500.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Great Himalayas (Himadri), also called the central axial range, extends for about 2,500 km from east to west. (महान हिमालय / हिमाद्रि)

 

• It is the northernmost and most continuous range of the Himalayas, with an average height of about 6,000 metres.

 

• It contains the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga, and Makalu.

 

• The range is composed mainly of granite and remains snow-covered throughout the year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Himalayas are conventionally divided into three parallel ranges: Himadri (Great Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser/Middle Himalayas), and the Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas).

 

• The average width of the Great Himalayan range is about 25 km.

 

NOTE

 

• 2800 (Option 1): not the standard textbook figure for the Great Himalayan range's length.

 

• 3000 (Option 3): overstates the accepted length of the range.

 

• 2100 (Option 4): understates the accepted length of the range.

question: What is the name of the mascot for 36th National Games, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mascot for the 36th National Games (2022), held in Gujarat, was named "Savaj," meaning "lion" in Gujarati. (सावज - एशियाई शेर, 36वें राष्ट्रीय खेलों का शुभंकर)

 

• Savaj is modelled on the Asiatic Lion, found only in the Gir forests of Gujarat.

 

• The mascot and anthem were launched by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

 

• The 36th National Games were held from 29 September to 12 October 2022 across multiple cities in Gujarat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 National Games (36th edition) were originally scheduled for 2021 but were postponed.

 

• Services (SSCB) topped the medal tally at the 36th National Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Chanakya (Option 1): not the mascot of the 36th National Games.

 

• Kojima (Option 2): not associated with the 36th National Games.

 

• Manikarnika (Option 3): not the mascot of the 36th National Games.

question:
Identify the person from the given statements.
He founded e-commerce giant Amazon in 1994 out of his garage in Seattle. He stepped down as CEO to become executive chairman in July 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jeff Bezos.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994 out of his garage in Bellevue/Seattle, Washington, initially as an online bookstore. (जेफ बेजोस - अमेज़न के संस्थापक)

 

• He stepped down as CEO of Amazon in July 2021, handing over the role to Andy Jassy, and became Executive Chairman.

 

• Amazon grew from an online bookstore into one of the world's largest e-commerce and cloud-computing (AWS) companies.

 

• Bezos also founded the aerospace company Blue Origin in 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jeff Bezos is one of the wealthiest individuals in the world, with his fortune closely tied to Amazon's growth.

 

• Amazon was originally going to be named "Cadabra" before being renamed.

 

NOTE

 

• Jack Ma (Option 1): founder of Alibaba Group, a Chinese e-commerce company, not Amazon.

 

• Steve Jobs (Option 2): co-founder of Apple Inc., not Amazon.

 

• Elon Musk (Option 4): CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, not the founder of Amazon.

question: Western ghats are locally known as _______ in Maharashtra.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sahyadri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Western Ghats are locally known as "Sahyadri" in Maharashtra. (सह्याद्रि - महाराष्ट्र में पश्चिमी घाट का स्थानीय नाम)

 

• They run parallel to the western coast of India, from the Tapi River in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.

 

• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised as one of the world's eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity.

 

• Different local names are used in different states: Sahyadri (Maharashtra), Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu/Karnataka border), Anaimalai and Cardamom Hills (Kerala).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The highest peak of the Western Ghats is Anamudi (2,695 m), located in Kerala.

 

• The Western Ghats are older than the Himalayan mountains.

 

NOTE

 

• Vindhya (Option 2): refers to the Vindhya Range, which divides North and South India — unrelated to the Western Ghats.

 

• Khadar (Option 3): refers to the newer, fertile floodplain alluvium of the Gangetic plains, unrelated to the Western Ghats.

 

• Gondwana (Option 4): refers to the ancient supercontinent from which the Indian peninsula broke away, not a local name for the Western Ghats.

question: If there are N firms in the economy, each assigned with a serial number from 1 to N, then as per the product method, GDP can be written as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is GVA1 + GVA2 ..... + GVAN.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the product method (value-added method), GDP is calculated as the sum of the Gross Value Added (GVA) of all producing units/firms in the economy. (उत्पादन विधि - सकल मूल्य वर्धित का योग)

 

• If there are N firms, numbered 1 to N, GDP = GVA1 + GVA2 + ..... + GVAN.

 

• GVA of a firm = Value of Output − Intermediate Consumption.

 

• This method avoids the problem of double counting by considering only the value added at each stage of production.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other two methods of estimating national income are the Income Method (sum of factor incomes) and the Expenditure Method (sum of final expenditures).

 

• GDP at market price = GVA at basic prices + taxes on products − subsidies on products.

 

NOTE

 

• GVA1 – GVA2 ..... – GVAN (Option 1): incorrect; the GVAs of different firms are added together, not subtracted.

 

• NVA1 + NVA2 ..... + NVAN (Option 2): incorrect; the product method sums Gross Value Added (GVA), not Net Value Added (NVA).

 

• GVA1 + NVA2 + GVA3 + NVA4 ..... (Option 4): incorrect; it inconsistently mixes gross and net value-added terms.

question: National Highways Infra Trust (NHAI InvIT) bonds introduced by Union Minister of Transport and Highways in October 2022 will provide a effective yield of ______ percent each year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.05.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Highways Infra Trust (NHAI InvIT) launched retail bonds (NCDs) in October 2022, offering an effective annual yield of 8.05 percent. (एनएचएआई इनविट बांड)

 

• The bonds were introduced under the Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, led by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari.

 

• NHAI InvIT is an Infrastructure Investment Trust set up by the National Highways Authority of India to monetise operational national highway stretches through the Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) model.

 

• The bond issue aimed to attract retail investors into infrastructure financing for national highway projects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NHAI InvIT was India's first infrastructure investment trust sponsored by a government entity.

 

• The bonds were structured to provide steady annual/periodic interest payouts to investors.

 

NOTE

 

• 6.05 percent (Option 1): incorrect; lower than the actual offered yield.

 

• 9.05 percent (Option 2): incorrect; higher than the actual offered yield.

 

• 7.05 percent (Option 3): incorrect; lower than the actual offered yield.

question: India won the only bronze medal in which team sports at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian men's hockey team won the bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), India's only team-sport medal at that edition. (भारतीय पुरुष हॉकी टीम - कांस्य पदक)

 

• India defeated Germany 5-4 in the bronze medal match.

 

• This was India's first Olympic hockey medal since the 1980 Moscow Olympics, ending a 41-year medal drought in the sport.

 

• PR Sreejesh, the Indian goalkeeper, played a crucial role in India's victory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India won a total of 7 medals at Tokyo Olympics 2020 — 1 gold (Neeraj Chopra, javelin throw), 2 silver, and 4 bronze.

 

• The Indian women's hockey team also had a historic run, finishing fourth (their best-ever Olympic result at that time).

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): India did not win a medal in table tennis at Tokyo 2020.

 

• Basketball (Option 2): India did not qualify for basketball at the Tokyo Olympics.

 

• Badminton (Option 4): Badminton is an individual sport; P.V. Sindhu won an individual bronze medal, not a team-sport medal.

question: What is the average height of inner Himalayas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6000 metres.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The inner Himalayas, also known as the Great Himalayas or Himadri, have an average height of about 6,000 metres. (हिमाद्रि - महान हिमालय, औसत ऊँचाई 6000 मीटर)

 

• This range contains the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest (8,848.86 m) and Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).

 

• It is the northernmost, continuous, and most rugged range of the Himalayan system.

 

• The range remains permanently snow-covered due to its high average elevation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) lie south of the Great Himalayas, with average elevations of 3,700-4,500 metres.

 

• The outermost range, the Shiwaliks, has a much lower average elevation of 900-1,100 metres.

 

NOTE

 

• 4500 metres (Option 2): closer to the average height of the Lesser/Middle Himalayas (Himachal), not the Great Himalayas.

 

• 5200 metres (Option 3): does not match the accepted average height of the Great Himalayan range.

 

• 7100 metres (Option 4): overstates the average height; this figure exceeds the standard textbook value.

question: Article 350A of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
option_2: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage
option_3: Direction for development of the Hindi language
option_4: Language to be used in Supreme Court and High Courts of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 350A of the Indian Constitution directs every State and local authority to provide facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups. (अनुच्छेद 350क - मातृभाषा में शिक्षा)

 

• It was inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.

 

• It reflects the State's duty to protect linguistic minorities and preserve linguistic diversity in education.

 

• The President may issue directions to a State as deemed necessary for securing this provision.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities.

 

• Article 351 deals with the direction for the development of the Hindi language.

 

NOTE

 

• Special officers for linguistic minorities (Option 1): this is the subject of Article 350B, not 350A.

 

• Direction for development of the Hindi language (Option 3): this is the subject matter of Article 351.

 

• Language to be used in Supreme Court and High Courts of India (Option 4): this is dealt with under Article 348, not Article 350A.

question: What is the percentage of carbon dioxide in the air exhaled by human lungs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.4 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The air exhaled by human lungs contains approximately 4.4 percent carbon dioxide, compared to only about 0.04 percent CO₂ in normal atmospheric air. (साँस से बाहर निकलने वाली हवा में कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड)

 

• Exhaled air also contains about 16 percent oxygen (compared to about 21 percent in inhaled atmospheric air).

 

• This exchange occurs in the alveoli of the lungs, where oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out to be exhaled.

 

• The elevated CO₂ content is a product of cellular respiration occurring throughout the body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exhaled air also contains water vapour and a small amount of nitrogen and inert gases, similar to inhaled air.

 

• Rising atmospheric CO₂ levels are separately tracked as an indicator of climate change (currently over 400 ppm, i.e., about 0.04%).

 

NOTE

 

• 3.2 percent (Option 1): underestimates the actual CO₂ percentage in exhaled air.

 

• 5.9 percent (Option 2): overestimates the standard textbook value for CO₂ in exhaled air.

 

• 2.3 percent (Option 3): underestimates the actual CO₂ percentage in exhaled air.

question: Which Indian cricketer is also known as Little Master?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunil Gavasker.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sunil Gavaskar, the former Indian cricket captain and opening batsman, is popularly known as the "Little Master." (सुनील गावस्कर - लिटिल मास्टर)

 

• He was the first batsman in cricket history to score 10,000 runs in Test cricket.

 

• He scored 34 Test centuries, a world record that stood until Sachin Tendulkar surpassed it in 2005.

 

• Gavaskar played 125 Test matches for India between 1971 and 1987 and is regarded as one of the greatest opening batsmen in cricket history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sachin Tendulkar is often referred to as the "Master Blaster."

 

• Gavaskar was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1980 and later inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame.

 

NOTE

 

• Umesh Yadav (Option 1): an Indian fast bowler, not known by this nickname.

 

• Virat Kohli (Option 2): former Indian cricket captain, known by nicknames like "Chase Master" or "King Kohli," not "Little Master."

 

• Kapil Dev (Option 4): legendary Indian all-rounder, known as the "Haryana Hurricane," not "Little Master."

question: When was Alluri Sitarama Raju arrested ending a two-year armed tribal struggle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is May 1924.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju, the tribal leader of the Rampa Rebellion (1922-1924) in the Godavari agency area (present-day Andhra Pradesh), was captured by the British in May 1924, ending his two-year armed struggle. (अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू - रम्पा विद्रोह)

 

• He led tribal groups against British forest laws that restricted their traditional podu (shifting) cultivation and access to forest resources.

 

• He was popularly known as "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungles).

 

• He was executed by the British shortly after his capture, on 7 May 1924.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rampa Rebellion is also called the "Manyam Rebellion."

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju's life and struggle inspired parts of the 2022 Telugu film "RRR," and he remains a folk hero in Andhra Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• January 1921 (Option 2): does not mark the end of the Rampa Rebellion; the rebellion was still ongoing during this period.

 

• April 1919 (Option 3): predates the start of the Rampa Rebellion (1922).

 

• December 1929 (Option 4): well after Alluri Sitarama Raju's capture and execution in 1924.

question: Which Indian festival celebrates the birth anniversary of spiritual leader Padmasambhava, founder of Tibet Tantric Buddhism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hemis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hemis festival, celebrated at the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh, marks the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), the founder of Tibetan Tantric Buddhism. (हेमिस उत्सव - पद्मसंभव की जयंती)

 

• It is celebrated on the 10th day of the fifth month of the Tibetan lunar calendar.

 

• The festival features masked "Cham" dances performed by monks, depicting the victory of good over evil.

 

• Hemis Monastery, founded in 1630, is the largest and wealthiest monastery in Ladakh, belonging to the Drukpa lineage of Tibetan Buddhism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Every 12 years, a large thangka (sacred scroll painting) of Padmasambhava is displayed at Hemis Monastery.

 

• Padmasambhava is credited with introducing Vajrayana Buddhism to Tibet and Bhutan in the 8th century CE.

 

NOTE

 

• Bakrid (Option 1): an Islamic festival (Eid al-Adha) commemorating the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son — unrelated to Padmasambhava.

 

• Losar (Option 2): the Tibetan/Ladakhi New Year festival, not specifically linked to Padmasambhava's birth anniversary.

 

• Gurpurab (Option 3): a Sikh festival commemorating the birth anniversaries of Sikh Gurus, unrelated to Padmasambhava.
